notes:
User is training for a fall sprint triathlon with about 12 weeks to prepare. Current fitness:
- Mixes cardio and strength training at the gym.
- Plays volleyball on weeknights and soccer on Sundays.
- Volleyball league team, the Net Ninjas, is currently 5–2.
- Can swim laps but swims slowly; wants to improve swimming technique and endurance.
- Limited running experience; recently ran a 5K in 32:15.
- Does not own a bike yet but plans to buy one soon; wants to develop beginner cycling skills.
- Primary triathlon priorities: swimming and biking, while maintaining running fitness.
- Interested in triathlon gear, technique, endurance, transitions, mobility/flexibility, strength, recovery, and injury prevention. Suggested additions: 1–2 short mobility sessions weekly, gradual volume, technique drills, brick workouts, transition practice, and recovery/nutrition planning.

Agreed general 12-week triathlon structure: base building, build/intensity, then taper. Suggested weekly priorities: 2–3 swims (technique/endurance), 2 bike sessions (long ride plus intervals/hills after bike acquisition), 1–2 easy runs, 1 strength session, and occasional bike-to-run bricks. A constrained layout considered: Tuesday swim, Wednesday longer ride, Friday easy run, Saturday second bike session/brick, with volleyball Monday/Thursday and soccer Sunday. Exact calendar should be finalized after confirming game times, available training days, medical history, and bike acquisition. A professional bike fitting was considered desirable; location is still unknown, so ask for city/state or region and recommend certified reputable fitters/shops. Fitting guidance can include expected cost, what to bring, whether to fit before buying, and what bike sizing/comfort should be addressed.

User is also considering helping organize a recreational office basketball league. They plan to limit their workload by finding a co-organizer and scheduling basketball around triathlon training and rest. They will start with a survey to gauge colleague interest and determine participation/availability. Early league ideas include a suitable venue, flexible schedule, clear recreational format/rules, fair teams or skill-based divisions, communication channel, and sportsmanship. They plan to begin with group clinics and online resources for beginners or players wanting improvement, then reassess whether to add private coaching or practice sessions. They are considering prizes/recognition for winning teams, MVPs, most improved team, best team spirit, Player of the Week/Month, and possibly modest gifts, swag, or a team celebration. Keep prizes fun and secondary to camaraderie, define fair award criteria, and consider sponsors to reduce costs.

User wants to host a mini tournament to close the basketball season and invite friends from the volleyball league. Open question: whether to mix players/teams or keep original teams separate. Suggested hybrid approach: use mixed teams for a few round-robin/social games, then retain original teams for final rounds, balancing chemistry with new connections. A participant survey is a good way to decide. Basketball’s injury/energy demands should remain compatible with triathlon priorities and recovery.
